title: Settling a Decided Claim on a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
Money reaches a Travel Protection Plans policyholder on a claim through a single payment recorded against the certificate. This page states what that payment governs and how the desk records it.

## Applicable situation

The settlement arises on a certificate carrying a decision the insurer has allowed, where the allowed amount has not yet been paid.

A settlement is paid on a certificate only after its premium lines carry every rating component the certificate's declared particulars call for. Until the premium record stands complete in that sense, the certificate is not one on which a settlement is paid.

What is governed is the amount paid to the policyholder and the amount held back from it as a deductible. The payment is made against the benefit the decision was reached on, for one insured traveller named on the certificate, and what is held back is recorded beside it.

The benefit a settlement pays is fixed only after the benefit the certificate records as consumed carries a restoration for every amount a supplier has paid the traveller for a loss the certificate has already settled. The benefit consumed is the figure that settlement is measured against, and it is that figure as the certificate's records stand at the moment the settlement is worked out.

## Recording the settlement

The desk records the payment with the travel protection desk tool `settle_benefit_payment_411249ab`, which is not listed among the ordinary tools: the representative unlocks it and then calls it. One call records a single payment row against the named certificate, tied to the insurer's decision it settles, for the benefit named and the insured traveller named, stating the amount paid to the policyholder and the deductible held back from it. Once the call completes, the certificate's claim record shows that claim standing as paid, and the policyholder can see the payment and the amount held back on their claim statement.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `care_policy_id` | The reference number of the travel protection policy record the payment is made under | Read from the policy record returned by the policy finder |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the traveller profile the payment is made to | Read from the traveller profile returned by the profile finder |
| `source_claim_id` | The reference number of the insurer's decision row this payment settles | Read from the claim records returned by the claims finder |
| `claim_reference` | The claim reference the insurer quoted for the claim being paid | Taken unchanged from the claim record it is read on and copied character for character, keeping the original wording, digits, spacing and punctuation, with no translation, normalisation, summarisation, addition or deletion |
| `claim_type` | The benefit of the plan the payment is made against | Exactly one of the eleven benefits below, and never anything else |
| `insured_sequence` | Which insured traveller named on the certificate the payment belongs to | A whole number starting at 1 counted in the order the travellers are named, with no decimal part, never left empty |
| `paid_amount_usd` | The amount actually paid to the policyholder | A USD amount with 2 decimal places, always positive, rounded half to even at the cent; held in US dollars whatever currency it is paid in, never left empty |
| `deductible_applied_usd` | The amount held back from the payment | A USD amount with 2 decimal places, zero or positive, rounded half to even at the cent; where nothing is held back it is given as 0.00 rather than left empty |

The eleven benefits the `claim_type` parameter accepts are `trip_cancellation`, where the journey was given up before it began; `trip_interruption`, where the journey was cut short once it had begun; `medical_emergency`, where the traveller needed emergency medical treatment away from home; `dental_emergency`, where the traveller needed emergency dental treatment away from home; `evacuation`, where the traveller had to be moved to care or repatriated; `baggage_delay`, where the traveller's baggage arrived late and essentials had to be bought; `baggage_loss`, where the traveller's baggage or an article in it was lost or damaged; `travel_delay`, where a booked departure ran late and the traveller was out of pocket; `missed_connection`, where a late arrival caused an onward booked service to be missed; `rental_damage`, where a hired vehicle was damaged while the traveller held it; and `cancel_for_any_reason`, where the journey was given up for a reason the listed causes do not name, on a plan carrying that benefit.

## Return

The call returns a single confirmation sentence naming the reference number of the payment row created, which is a text reference beginning ccp_, the reference number of the certificate it was recorded against, the amount paid in US dollars to two decimal places and the amount held back in US dollars to two decimal places. The presence of the new payment reference in that sentence is what indicates the payment was recorded; there is no other success flag.
